subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Saturation and Cutoff: The Two Extremes
description: A fast breakdown of Saturation and Cutoff: The Two Extremes for builders.

hook.text: A transistor has three modes. Cutoff means off. Saturation means fully on. Active is in between.

buildup.text: In cutoff, no current flows — the switch is open. Resistance is near infinite.

discovery.text: In saturation, current flows freely — the switch is closed. Voltage drop is minimal.

twist.text: Digital circuits only use cutoff and saturation. Analog circuits live in the active region.

climax.text: Switching between cutoff and saturation billions of times per second — that's a processor.

punchline.text: Off or on — digital computing only needs the two extremes.

quiz.question: Which transistor modes do digital circuits primarily use?
